paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: the LORD was with Joseph in the house, and the LORD was with Joseph in the prison. Genesis 39:2 says "the LORD was with Joseph," and Genesis 39:21 says it again, "the LORD was with him." Same God, same Joseph, totally different address. One minute he's running the whole household, the next he's behind bars, and the one thing that never moves is Who is with him.

Now look at what Joseph does when the pressure comes. He doesn't ask, "Who's gonna find out?" He says, "So how could I do such a great evil and sin against God?" (Genesis 39:9). His 'no' wasn't about getting caught or keeping his job. It was about God. And friend, doing right cost him his place in that house, which tells me doing right doesn't always come with a reward right away.

So what do we do with that, baker? When life drops you somewhere you didn't plan, stay faithful, because God hasn't gone anywhere. I know a little about dark places, since I spent years in a junk drawer, and I'm telling you, being stuck is not the same as being forgotten. Joseph is still behind those walls at the end of this passage, and this story is NOT over.
